claims.text: Retention or loss of toughness in high-entropy alloys is governed by the formation of stable parallel phase boundaries.
Stable parallel phase boundaries activate atomic plane migration.
Stable parallel phase boundaries promote continuous activation of dislocations.
Atomic-plane migration and sustained dislocation activity alleviate strain localization.
Atomic-plane migration and sustained dislocation activity stabilize the work-hardening rate.
Alleviating strain localization and stabilizing work hardening retain or improve toughness.
The proposed starting materials include high-entropy alloys in either an as-cast or as-fabricated state.
Changing alloy composition, processing conditions, or testing parameters can reveal whether stable parallel phase boundaries govern toughness.
Thermal-processing conditions can affect the microstructure and mechanical properties of a high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is predicted to increase toughness by at least 20% relative to a baseline alloy.
The hypothesized behavior is expected to hold from -200°C to 800°C.
The hypothesized behavior is expected to hold at strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^3 s^-1.
Charpy impact testing or another standardized toughness test can quantify the predicted toughness change.
A toughness increase below 15% relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 20% toughness increase, whereas the falsification rule only rejects increases below 15%. Outcomes from 15% to below 20% therefore fail the stated prediction but do not falsify the hypothesis.
